settings.description: How many requests a Run admits in a minute at most, spaced evenly (GCRA), whatever its concurrency; none by default. An Operator policy cap bounds it even when unset, and a run already going takes a tightened cap at its next admission.
settings.name: admission.max_requests_per_minute

settings.description: The resource kinds the Session's pages never load, failed as `BlockedByClient` by its interception before every navigation: any of `image`, `media`, `font` and `stylesheet`; none by default. The never-block list still loads a challenge's own. In `standard` and `stealth` the Run warns once per Session that the site can see the missing loads.
settings.name: browser.block_resources

settings.description: Whether the Session's Chromium runs with no window: `true` by default. Headless or not, the site sees one browser's identity, with no `HeadlessChrome` token in its user agent.
settings.name: browser.headless

settings.description: How long a Pinned artifact no installed executable pins stays in the Browser cache unused before the clean-up deletes it, and how long an executable's entry counts as installed after it was last seen: 30 days. `null` turns the automatic clean-up off. Set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.
settings.name: browser_cache.max_unused_age

settings.description: How often a live Run writes a Checkpoint where the engine keeps its Checkpoints, on the engine's clock; none by default locally.
settings.name: checkpoint.interval

settings.description: The domains whose consent prompts a run accepts instead of refusing. A Recipe or a run only narrows it; it is widened only in configuration or by a person's answer.
settings.name: consent.domains

settings.description: Where the Daemon serves the Console, as `host:port`: `127.0.0.1` on port 7800 plus the major (7700 plus the minor during `0.y` previews), so each major's Console has its own port. Port 0 takes a free port, which the Daemon's runtime file and `daemon status` report. Set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.
settings.name: console.address

settings.description: Where the Daemon serves the Console's content origin, which shows scraped HTML, screenshots, DOM snapshots and page bodies, as `host:port`. None by default: the Console's host on a free port, or, when `console.content_public_url` is set, the Console's own listener, which tells the two origins apart by the `Host` each request names. Set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.
settings.name: console.content_address

settings.description: The origin a browser reaches the Console's content origin at behind a proxy, such as `https://content.example.com`, which the addresses the Console signs name. None by default: the content origin's own listener. With no `console.content_address`, the content origin shares the Console's listener and answers the requests that name this origin's host. Set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.
settings.name: console.content_public_url

settings.description: How long a Console sign-in lasts without being used, in milliseconds: 30 days. Each use starts it again; a sign-in unused for longer ends, and its person signs in again. Set in an Operator policy only.
settings.name: console.sign_in.idle_expiry

settings.description: How many times one address may try to sign in to the Console in a minute: 10. A further attempt in that minute is refused, whatever its credential. Set in an Operator policy only.
settings.name: console.sign_in.rate

settings.description: Host names, each with the domain key its requests and those of the hosts under it share, the longest name winning, in place of the registrable domain under the Public Suffix List: a Recipe's override of the key its per-domain queues use. None by default.
settings.name: crawl.domain_keys

settings.description: How many work items the program's handler is given at once: 16, Scrapy's `CONCURRENT_REQUESTS`. A run already going takes a tightened Operator policy cap at its next admission.
settings.name: crawl.handler.concurrency

settings.description: Whether a crawl's Run stays `running` with an empty Frontier and nothing in flight, waiting for new work, until `run.finish` lets it end once its work items are done: `false`, so a crawl finishes once its work items are done. Its idle time counts toward `timeout.run`, and an abort stops it as any Run.
settings.name: crawl.keep_alive

settings.description: How deep a crawl goes, its seeds at depth 0 and each enqueue one level deeper than the request whose attempt added it: a deeper request is not added, with `max_depth`, and a Run that refused one ends `incomplete`. None by default; `null` clears it.
settings.name: crawl.max_depth

settings.description: The most segments a URL's path may have, as the WHATWG parser splits it, an empty last segment (a trailing slash) not counted (Heritrix's `maxPathDepth`): a URL with more is not added, with `max_path_segments`, and a finished Run that refused one is `unverified`. 20 by default; `null` turns the cap off.
settings.name: crawl.max_path_segments

settings.description: How many requests a crawl admits, its seeds included: once it admitted this many, a further one is not added, with `max_requests`, and a Run that refused one ends `incomplete`. None by default; `null` clears it.
settings.name: crawl.max_requests

settings.description: How many times back to back a segment of a URL's path, or a run of segments, may appear (Heritrix's `maxRepetitions`), so `/a/a` passes and `/a/a/a` and `/a/b/a/b/a/b` do not, while numbers that recur apart, as in `/page/1/tag/1/sort/1`, do: a URL past it is not added, with `max_segment_repeats`, and a finished Run that refused one is `unverified`. 2 by default; `null` turns the cap off.
settings.name: crawl.max_segment_repeats

settings.description: The longest URL a crawl admits, in characters as the WHATWG parser serializes it, without its fragment (Scrapy's `URLLENGTH_LIMIT`): a longer one is not added, with `max_url_length`, and a finished Run that refused one is `unverified`. 2,083 by default; `null` turns the cap off.
settings.name: crawl.max_url_length

settings.description: Whether a work item whose handler failed with `handler_failed` is tried again: `false`.
settings.name: crawl.retry.handler_failed

settings.description: How many times a work item whose attempt failed retryably is tried again: 2, Scrapy's `RETRY_TIMES`. A run already going takes a tightened Operator policy cap before its next retry.
settings.name: crawl.retry.max

settings.description: How many pages the sample crawl visits.
settings.name: crawl.sample_pages

settings.description: URL patterns, each a glob read as Playwright reads one and matched in the engine, none of which a link may match, besides `crawl.scope.strategy` and `crawl.scope.include`. None by default. Fixed for a Run's life.
settings.name: crawl.scope.exclude

settings.description: URL patterns, each a glob read as Playwright reads one and matched in the engine, of which a link must match one when there are any, besides `crawl.scope.strategy`, which they never replace. None by default. Fixed for a Run's life.
settings.name: crawl.scope.include

settings.description: What a crawl's links are measured by against every seed, on every enqueue, redirect and Hook rewrite: `same_hostname` (Crawlee's default), `same_domain` (the registrable domain under the Public Suffix List), `same_origin` or `all`. One leading `www.` label is ignored, and under `same_origin` an `http` seed also admits its host's `https` origin on the same port. A link outside it is not added with `out_of_scope`. Fixed for a Run's life.
settings.name: crawl.scope.strategy

settings.description: Where `daemon run`, the foreground Daemon, listens, as `host:port`: `127.0.0.1` on port 7900 plus the major (7600 plus the minor during `0.y` previews). Port 0 takes a free port, which its log names. Only a loopback address, until the Daemon terminates TLS. Set in user configuration or an Operator policy, or for `daemon run` through `GOODFETCH_DAEMON_ADDRESS`.
settings.name: daemon.address

settings.description: How long `daemon run`, the foreground Daemon, drains on `SIGTERM` before it exits: 110 seconds, below the 120-second `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` of the Helm chart, which must exceed it. Each run that reaches its next safe point in that time stops with a Checkpoint, resumable by its Run ID; one that does not stays resumable from its run file. Set in user configuration or an Operator policy, or for `daemon run` through `GOODFETCH_DAEMON_DRAIN_GRACE` in milliseconds.
settings.name: daemon.drain_grace

settings.description: How long a Daemon with no connected Client, a visible Console tab included, waits before it stops: 10 minutes. `daemon start --keep-alive`, a held Schedule and an installed service keep it running. Set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.
settings.name: daemon.idle_timeout

settings.description: Every delivery reports its Guarantee class, an honesty guarantee that stays locked whatever the layer.
settings.name: delivery.report_guarantee_class

settings.description: Every write a Sink makes carries its delivery ID and run epoch, an honesty guarantee that stays locked whatever the layer.
settings.name: delivery.write_ids_and_epochs

settings.description: The hosts a run's requests may reach: each entry its host and their subdomains, matched on the host as a browser's URL parser leaves it (punycode, dotted-decimal IPv4), and `*` every host, only when written. `["*"]` by default; set for a connection or a Run. A request to a host it does not list fails with `egress_refused`.
settings.name: egress.allowed_domains

settings.description: The hosts no request of a run may reach, whatever `egress.allowed_domains` allows: each entry its host and their subdomains, matched as `egress.allowed_domains` matches, and `*` every host. Empty by default; set for a connection or a Run. A request to a host it lists fails with `egress_refused`.
settings.name: egress.blocked_domains

settings.description: Whether the engine opens no connection nobody configured: every pinned download, such as a Pinned artifact missing from the Browser cache, fails with `artifact_unavailable_offline` before it connects, naming the command that supplies it beforehand. `false` by default; set at every layer, and an Operator policy can lock it.
settings.name: egress.offline

settings.description: Whether a browser Session blocks ads by EasyList, as a blocker does: on by default in every Access mode. A blocked request fails as `BlockedByClient`; the never-block list keeps challenge, anti-bot, anti-fraud and payment scripts loading.
settings.name: filter_lists.ads

settings.description: Whether a browser Session blocks page annoyances (social widgets, newsletter and notification prompts) by Fanboy Annoyance, its cookie sections left to the Consent prompt runner: on by default in every Access mode.
settings.name: filter_lists.annoyances

settings.description: Extra Filter lists, by URL or path. Their scriptlets run only when the value comes from an Operator policy or user or project configuration; from a Recipe or a run, only their blocking rules apply.
settings.name: filter_lists.extra

settings.description: Whether a site's own scripts load whatever the Filter lists say: off by default.
settings.name: filter_lists.first_party_scripts

settings.description: Whether the Filter lists' scriptlets that patch a page's JavaScript run, from uBlock Origin's resources downloaded with the lists that name them: off by default, since a site can see them.
settings.name: filter_lists.page_scriptlets

settings.description: Whether a browser Session blocks trackers by EasyPrivacy: on by default in every Access mode. A blocked request fails as `BlockedByClient`; the never-block list keeps challenge, anti-bot, anti-fraud and payment scripts loading.
settings.name: filter_lists.trackers

settings.description: How many of a Run's Sessions share one browser process, each in a browser context of its own: 8. The Run's next Session past it gets a process of its own; Sessions of different Runs never share one.
settings.name: governor.browser.contexts_per_process

settings.description: The memory, in bytes, of a browser and its processes past which it is recycled; unset by default, when the cap is twice what the browser used once it had opened its first page.
settings.name: governor.browser.memory_cap

settings.description: How long a browser may hold no open page before it closes, each of its Sessions keeping its cookies and storage for the browser that replaces it: 5 minutes.
settings.name: governor.browser.recycle_idle

settings.description: How many pages a browser opens before it is recycled: 100. Recycled, it opens no new page, closes once its pages are done and is replaced, each of its Sessions keeping its cookies and storage.
settings.name: governor.browser.recycle_pages

settings.description: The most browser pages the engine's Resource governor admits open at once, across its Runs: 32.
settings.name: governor.browser_page.ceiling

settings.description: The fewest browser pages the engine's Resource governor keeps admitting at once, however loaded the machine: 1. Equal to `governor.browser_page.ceiling`, it fixes the concurrency there.
settings.name: governor.browser_page.floor

settings.description: The share of the Memory allowance in use, in percent, from which the engine's memory is critical: 95.
settings.name: governor.critical

settings.description: The most HTTP and discovered-API fetches the engine's Resource governor admits at once, across its Runs: 200.
settings.name: governor.http.ceiling

settings.description: The fewest HTTP and discovered-API fetches the engine's Resource governor keeps admitting at once, however loaded the machine: 1. Equal to `governor.http.ceiling`, it fixes the concurrency there.
settings.name: governor.http.floor

settings.description: How long the engine's memory may stay critical with its concurrency at the floor before the Resource governor reaches its last resort, when a Daemon's `/readyz` fails: 60 s.
settings.name: governor.last_resort_after

settings.description: The most memory, in bytes, the engine and its children may use, as its Memory allowance when it is tighter than the process's own cgroup limit, its Windows Job object's limit or half of physical memory; unset by default. Read again at every sample.
settings.name: governor.memory_allowance

settings.description: The most model calls the engine's Resource governor admits at once, across its Runs: 16.
settings.name: governor.model_call.ceiling

settings.description: The fewest model calls the engine's Resource governor keeps admitting at once, however loaded the machine: 1. Equal to `governor.model_call.ceiling`, it fixes the concurrency there.
settings.name: governor.model_call.floor

settings.description: The share of the Memory allowance in use, in percent, from which the engine is under pressure and its Resource governor lowers its concurrency; also the CPU and Tokio workers' busy share from which they hold it: 85.
settings.name: governor.pressure

settings.description: The share, in percent, of each kind's concurrency one Run may hold at once, at least one: 100. An Operator policy cap bounds every Run's share.
settings.name: governor.run_share

settings.description: How often the engine's Resource governor reads memory, CPU and Tokio saturation, sizes its concurrency and sends `engine.system_info`: every second.
settings.name: governor.sample_interval

settings.description: How many log files an engine process keeps where `log.output` is `file`, the one it writes included: 5, so a Daemon's logs stay under about 50 MiB. The oldest goes at each rotation. Read when the process starts; set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.
settings.name: log.file.max_files

settings.description: The size, in bytes, at which an engine process's log file rotates where `log.output` is `file`: 10 MiB. A file holds at most this much and one line more. Read when the process starts; set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.
settings.name: log.file.max_size

settings.description: How an engine process writes its logs on stderr, or on stdout under `daemon run`: `text`, lines for a person reading a terminal, or `json`, JSON lines. Unset, the logs are text on stderr and JSON lines on stdout under `daemon run`; a log file holds JSON lines whatever it says. Set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.
settings.name: log.format

settings.description: Which of its logs an engine process writes: `info`, the default, which logs state changes only (a Run started, resumed or stopped, a domain backing off, a storage level changing, a Daemon draining) and never one line per request, or any `tracing` filter directive, such as `warn` or `info,goodfetch::rpc=debug`. Read when the process starts; set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.
settings.name: log.level

settings.description: Where an engine process writes its logs beside stderr: `stdout`, JSON lines for the platform to collect and rotate, `file`, JSON lines in its own files of the Goodfetch home's log folder, rotated at `log.file.max_size` and kept to `log.file.max_files`, or `none`. Unset, it is `stdout` under `daemon run`, `file` for every other Daemon and `none` for an Attached engine, whose logs go to its Client as log events; `stdout` on an Attached engine, whose stdout is its protocol, fails with `setting_not_applicable`. Read when the process starts; set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.
settings.name: log.output

settings.description: Host names mapped to addresses before any lookup, in the engine's resolver and in Chromium, each address still checked by ADR 0017's resolved-address rule. Empty by default; an Operator policy can lock it.
settings.name: network.resolve

settings.description: Where `daemon run`, the foreground Daemon, serves its ops listener, as `host:port`: `/livez` and `/readyz` answer a status and no body to anyone, and `/metrics`, Prometheus' text, only with the ops token, the `ops.token` file of the major's folder, as a bearer token. Unset by default: no ops listener and no Prometheus export. Any address, so a cluster's probes and scrapers reach it; a request whose `Host` is a name other than `localhost`, or that carries an `Origin`, is refused. Set in user configuration or an Operator policy, or for `daemon run` through `GOODFETCH_OPS_ADDRESS`.
settings.name: ops.address

settings.description: The OTLP/HTTP endpoint `daemon run`, the foreground Daemon, exports its metrics to, in protobuf, every 60 seconds and once more as it exits: a full URL such as `http://collector:4318/v1/metrics`. Unset by default: nothing is exported (ADR 0043).
settings.name: otlp.metrics_endpoint

settings.description: The OTLP/HTTP endpoint an engine process exports its `tracing` spans to, such as `http://localhost:4318/v1/traces`; unset, the default, exports nothing, and nothing leaves the machine. The spans cover each run, page and CDP command, with glossary IDs and bounded values as fields and a URL as its origin. Span names, span fields and the engine's targets are Experimental: a minor may change them, and its release notes list the change. Set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.
settings.name: otlp.traces_endpoint

settings.description: The RPC endpoint of each chain whose finalized state proves a payment did not settle, by chain. Set only in an Operator policy and user and project configuration.
settings.name: paid_fetch.chain_rpc_endpoints

settings.description: The registrable domains a run may pay for a page; `*` only when written. Widened only in an Operator policy, user or project configuration, or by a person's answer; a Recipe or a run only narrows it.
settings.name: paid_fetch.domains

settings.description: The fixed rates that convert a price into a Limit's currency, by currency pair. Set only in an Operator policy and user and project configuration.
settings.name: paid_fetch.exchange_rates

settings.description: The most a run pays for one page, as an amount and its currency such as `0.05 USD`; none by default. Raised only in configuration; a Recipe or a run only lowers it.
settings.name: paid_fetch.max_price_per_page

settings.description: Whether a domain that answers 429, 502, 503 or 504, or does not answer in time, is backed off, and its `Retry-After` waited out, for every run of the user that shares Politeness. Off, the run ignores both, and it is listed in the run's result.
settings.name: politeness.backoff.enabled

settings.description: The shortest wait of a domain's backoff: each wait is drawn at random between it and three times the previous wait (the first between it and three times it), never above `politeness.backoff.max`: 2 s. A shorter value is listed in the run's result.
settings.name: politeness.backoff.initial

settings.description: The longest wait of a domain's backoff: 60 s. A `Retry-After` may hold the domain longer, up to `politeness.retry_after.max`. A shorter value is listed in the run's result.
settings.name: politeness.backoff.max

settings.description: How many requests may be in flight at once on one domain key, counted across every run of the user that shares Politeness: a run admits one only while that combined count is below its own value. None by default until the fetch tiers set ADR 0086's default of 1.
settings.name: politeness.domain.concurrency

settings.description: How long a run waits after the last request start on a domain key, by any run of the user that shares Politeness, before it starts another there. None by default until the fetch tiers set ADR 0086's default of 1 s.
settings.name: politeness.domain.delay

settings.description: The longest a crawl waits for the time a site's `Retry-After` asks, past `politeness.backoff.max`: 15 minutes. When the site asks for longer, nothing is sent to its domain before that time and nothing waits for it: the request whose response asked, and each request admitted to the domain meanwhile, ends `failed` with `response_unavailable`, and `run.retry_failed` re-admits them once the site is back. Whatever its value, nothing is sent sooner than the site asked.
settings.name: politeness.retry_after.max

settings.description: How a Run shares Politeness with the other runs of its user: `shared` with every engine of the user (through the Politeness store when one is configured, else on the machine), `per_daemon` on the machine only, ignoring a store, or `run` for Politeness of its own. Anything but `shared` is listed in the Run's result.
settings.name: politeness.sharing

settings.description: The hosts the Session reaches without its proxy, as Playwright's `bypass`: a comma-separated list such as `.example.com, chromium.org`, a leading dot naming a domain's subdomains. None by default: every request goes through `proxy.server`. Set as `proxy.server` is.
settings.name: proxy.bypass

settings.description: The Secret reference of the password the Session gives `proxy.server` with `proxy.username`, such as `env:PROXY_PASSWORD`: never a value, resolved when the Session opens and never written to a log, a trace, a process's arguments or a file. None by default. Set as `proxy.server` is.
settings.name: proxy.password

settings.description: The proxy every request of the Session goes through, as Playwright's `server`: an `http://`, `https://`, `socks5://` or `socks5h://` URL with a host and a port, such as `http://proxy.example:3128`. None by default: the machine's own address. Set on a Run, every Session of it takes it; set in `run.new_session`'s `settings`, that Session alone; a page or a request has no proxy of its own, so the address a site sees never changes under the same cookies. A URL carrying credentials and `socks4` are refused with `setting_invalid`: give the credentials as `proxy.username` and `proxy.password`. Set only by the program's own code, configuration and an Operator policy: a Recipe may expose it but never sets it, and a Client acting for a model is refused with `setting_locked`, since whoever sets it receives `proxy.password`. On Chromium, a SOCKS5 proxy's credentials go through a loopback relay the engine opens for the Session.
settings.name: proxy.server

value.description: A proxy URL, `http://`, `https://`, `socks5://` or `socks5h://`, with a host and an optional port and never credentials, such as `http://proxy.example:3128`.

settings.description: The username the Session gives `proxy.server`, as Playwright's `username`. None by default. Set as `proxy.server` is.
settings.name: proxy.username

settings.description: How long the engine's HTTP transports let a connection attempt to one of a host's addresses run before they start the next one beside it: 250 ms, RFC 8305's Connection Attempt Delay. An attempt that fails starts the next at once.
settings.name: resolver.attempt_delay

settings.description: How long the engine's HTTP transports wait for a host's IPv6 addresses once its IPv4 addresses arrived first, before they start connecting over IPv4: 50 ms, RFC 8305's Resolution Delay.
settings.name: resolver.resolution_delay

settings.description: How a Run's commits reach the disk: `full`, the default, keeps every acknowledged commit through a power cut (`synchronous=FULL`, with `fullfsync` on macOS); `fast` (`synchronous=NORMAL`) survives a process crash only, since an OS crash or a power cut may roll back recent commits, possibly many, without damaging the run state. A Run in `fast` names it in its run report's `weakened`.
settings.name: run_state.durability

settings.description: The Secret reference of the key-encryption key that wraps each Run's data key. One set in a layer is resolved when a Run starts: a Run whose reference does not resolve is refused with `secret_unavailable`. Taken only from an Operator policy and user and project configuration. By default the OS keychain's `keychain:goodfetch/run-state-key`, or, on a host with no OS keychain, the encrypted local file's `secretfile:run-state-key`, which `config explain` shows as the default it chose; the engine makes the default's item, a random 256-bit key, where it is missing when a Run first seals a field. A Run's data key is stored only wrapped by this key, so a resume, such as of a Checkpoint moved to another machine, unwraps it with the key this setting names for the resume, which a Client may send in `run.resume`'s project configuration: one that gives no value fails the resume with `secret_unavailable`, one that does not open the data key with `run_key_mismatch`. The encrypted local file, `secrets/<name>.age` in Goodfetch home encrypted with age to the X25519 identity in `secrets/identity.txt`, a file only its owner may read, protects copies and backups of the home, not the value from another process of the same user.
settings.name: run_state.key_reference

settings.description: Where Runs keep their run state: `per_run`, the default, one SQLite file in each run folder; `per_install`, one database, `run-state.sqlite` in the per-major folder, holding every Run of the install and major and written by the Daemon alone, to which an Attached engine then hands its Runs. Export, import and Checkpoint give the same per-run file in both. Taken only from the machine's own layers, and read when the Daemon starts.
settings.name: run_state.layout

settings.description: The folder that holds the run folders, each named by its Run ID; by default the per-user, per-major data folder of the Goodfetch home.
settings.name: run_state.location

settings.description: How many times the sample operation repeats a text.
settings.name: sample.echo_repeats

settings.description: Secrets are given by Secret reference, never as values, an honesty guarantee that stays locked whatever the layer.
settings.name: secrets.by_reference

settings.description: How long after it opened a Session of a crawl's Session pool is retired: 3,000 s, Crawlee's `maxAgeSecs`.
settings.name: session.pool.max_age

settings.description: The error score at which a Session of a crawl's Session pool is retired: 3. A block or a failed Page check adds 1, a success takes 0.5 off, never below 0 (Crawlee's model).
settings.name: session.pool.max_error_score

settings.description: How many Sessions a crawl's Session pool keeps open at once: 100. A request goes to a new Session while the pool has room, then to one drawn among those open.
settings.name: session.pool.max_size

settings.description: How many requests one Session of a crawl's Session pool serves before it is retired: 50, Crawlee's `maxUsageCount`.
settings.name: session.pool.max_uses

settings.description: Where a Session's login comes from: exactly one kind of ADR 0056's tagged union, or none for a fresh Session. Set at a Run or a connection, it is the default of the Sessions opened beneath; opening a Session takes its own as the call's `source`, and in that Session's own `settings` it is refused with `setting_not_applicable`. A Recipe never sets or locks it; it may only expose it to its users.
settings.name: session.source

settings.description: The free space, in bytes, below which a filesystem a Run writes to is at the `critical` storage level: every Run with an essential write on it stops resumably at its next safe point, with `resource: "storage"`, and a new Run whose run file would go there is refused with `resources_exhausted`. Read again at every sample of the Resource governor; set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.
settings.name: storage.low_free

settings.description: How long a locator action waits for its target to be unique and actionable, and replays a gesture that landed elsewhere, before it fails with `deadline_exceeded`, or `target_not_unique` for a target still ambiguous: 30 s.
settings.name: timeout.action

settings.description: How long a stop of a Run, `run.stop` or a scope's close, waits for its next safe point before it fails with `deadline_exceeded`, the Run still stopping there: 30 s.
settings.name: timeout.close

settings.description: How long a request may wait for its response's first byte before its attempt fails with `deadline_exceeded`: 30 s.
settings.name: timeout.first_byte

settings.description: How long a crawl's handler has for one attempt, which also bounds every action inside it, and from which a work item's lease is derived: the timeout plus the larger of 10 s and a tenth of it. 60 s, Crawlee's `requestHandlerTimeoutSecs`.
settings.name: timeout.handler

settings.description: How long a navigation may take before its attempt fails with `deadline_exceeded`: 30 s, Playwright's default.
settings.name: timeout.navigation

settings.description: How long a Run may go on before it checkpoints and stops at its next safe point, resumable; none by default.
settings.name: timeout.run

settings.description: How long a Secret provider may take to answer one reference before the resolution fails with `secret_unavailable`, `failure: "timed_out"`: 30 s.
settings.name: timeout.secret

settings.description: How long a wait for an application state, such as `page.wait_for_request_finished`, may take before it fails with `deadline_exceeded`: 30 s.
settings.name: timeout.wait

settings.description: Domains whose certificate may fail verification, each with a pin, `any`, or `null` for trust on first use. A pin and `any` are taken only from an Operator policy and user and project configuration; a Recipe or a run may list a domain only for trust on first use.
settings.name: tls.accept_invalid_certs

settings.description: Extra certificate authorities by domain: a host or a registrable domain with its subdomains, mapped to certificate files or Secret references, trusted beside the default roots for that domain and nowhere else. Taken only from an Operator policy and user and project configuration, never from a Recipe or a run; on a Daemon with accounts only the operator role writes it, in the Operator policy.
settings.name: tls.trusted_cas

settings.description: Whether an executable more than three months past its release date prints one line a day on stderr saying so, from its own release date alone, with no network call. Set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.

settings.description: The domains whose Walls no run reads past, whatever another layer allows. Set only in an Operator policy.
